newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian panel urges action on Aboriginal health.
newsitem.headline: Australian panel urges action on Aboriginal health.

text.p: A panel of medical experts has asked the Australian government to step up efforts to improve Aboriginal health, calling for a national plan of action.

The expert panel on indigenous health comprising members of the Australian Medical Association and Public Health Association of Australia said the federal government's policy of incremental progress was not good enough.

"The poor health of Aboriginal Australians must be viewed as a national crisis and our failure to deal with this issue is a stain on our national character at home and abroad," the statement said. The panel met Prime Minister John Howard, Health Minister Michael Wooldridge and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Affairs Minister John Herron in May and presented them with a submission outlining the current status of indigenous peoples' health. "We are impressed by their level of concern and their depth of understanding of the issues, but we believe more needs to be done," the panel said.

Australia's conservative Liberal-National coalition government has cut A$400 million (US$300 million) from indigenous spending over the next four years. The panel said a national plan of action needed to be drawn up which required the support of government and the community.

The panel said Aborigines had a much higher mortality rate than the rest of the population and probably the highest level of rheumatic fever in the world. The panel said Australia needed to learn from New Zealand and North American successes in dealing with the problems of indigenous peoples' health.
